application_type_full: Tree works: Trees in conservation areas/subject to TPOs
description: T4 Cherry: Fell to ground level and grind out the stumpOn the map provided online this tree is listed as Norway Maple when they are actually Cherry tree.Reasons for felling are in the arb report, Client has a replanting scheme also.Back in June I was a decision letter with 1 of the tree's proposed fell being accepted and 1 of the tree's proposed works being refused.An Arb report by the insurance company was provided with all necessary details and survey however the decision only relates to the amenity of the tree and not the effect the tree is having on the property as raised on the report. I have gone back to the site and collected even further evidence with pictures for your reference. my client the MOD has a responsibility for their trees to not affect non MOD properties which this tree is. please can the subsidence/health and safety of others being took into account instead of the amenity this tree provides.
decision_conditions: Any replacement trees which within a period of five years from planting are removed, die or become seriously damaged/diseased shall be replaced within the next planting season (Oct 1st to April 30th) with trees of similar amenity value.Any replacement planting should be carried out with due consideration for overhead and underground services, property boundaries, buildings and potential maintenance. The eventual size of a specimen and the nature of its rooting structure should also be taken into account when choosing where to plant, in order to achieve the best result for your site.{\b Plant one of the following from the list below as a replacement species.a) Cherry 'Pandora' (Prunus 'Pandora')b) Great White Cherry (Prunus 'Tai-haku')c) Tibetan Cherry (Prunus serrula) }I have to warn you that if one of the above specified replacements is not planted by the end of the first planting season (Oct 1st to April 30th) following the proposed removals, a notice may be served under section 207 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended). However, I trust that such action will not be necessary and I look forward to receiving your full cooperation in this matter. Please ensure that you inform the Council's Lead Tree Officer (james.baker@kingston.gov.uk) with the provision of a photo once the replanting has taken place.
